trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: IT Solutions Architect (Broader Africa Technology)
Company: FirstRand
Purpose of the role: To define, govern and implement technology solutions across the organisation's cross-border payments ecosystem, ensuring alignment with business strategy, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and enterprise architecture principles. Providing strategic technology solution leadership to support the modernisation the cross-border payment capability to ensure scalable, secure and resilient payment solutions are put in place to support the broader Africa business.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Define and maintain the target architecture for cross-border payments across the organisation
  - Develop solution architectures supporting payment hubs, SWIFT, ISO 20022, clearing networks, correspondent banking and cross-border settlement processes
  - Ensure technology solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, payment strategy and regulatory obligations
  - Establish and enforce architectural principles, standards and governance processes for the payments domain
  - Produce conceptual, logical and physical architecture artefacts which are continiously maintained.
  - Act as the architecture authority for all cross-border payment initiatives on platform
  - Maintain end-to-end visibility of payment journeys across customer channels, core banking systems, payment hubs, middleware and external payment networks that are part of the platforms ecosystem
  - Drive architecture decisions relating to: SWIFT FIN and ISO 20022 messaging, Cross-border payment processing, Correspondent banking integrations, Treasury and liquidity management integration, Foreign exchange processing, Sanctions and compliance screening, AML transaction monitoring, Real-time and near real-time payment capabilities
  - Collaborate with senior leadership to translate the business objectives into technology strategies and architectural solutions
  - Collaborate with integrating capability areas to ensure there is alignment on solutions and architectural roadmaps
Must-have requirements:
  - 10+ years in architecture focused on payment solutions
  - Financial banking experience
  - SWIFT Network exeperience (MX / MT)
  - Agentic AI
  - Enterprise Sparx
  - Bachelors in Computer science, information systems , Engineering or related field
Nice-to-have:
  - BIAN
  - Cloud (AWS, Azure)
  - TOGAF
  - SWIFT related qualifications
  - PASA
Location: Johannesburg
Closing date: 2026-11-09
Employment equity statement: All appointments will be made in line with FirstRand Group’s Employment Equity plan.
Accessibility statement: The Bank supports the recruitment and advancement of individuals with disabilities. In order for us to fulfill this purpose, candidates can disclose their disability information on a voluntary basis. The Bank will keep this information confidential unless we are required by law to disclose this information to other parties.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

IT Solutions Architect (Cross-Border Payments)

FirstRand

Johannesburg

About the role
You will define, govern and implement technology solutions across FirstRand's cross-border payments ecosystem. Your work keeps solutions aligned with business strategy, regulatory requirements, industry standards and enterprise architecture principles. You will provide the architecture leadership behind the modernisation of the cross-border payment capability, so that scalable, secure and resilient payment solutions support the broader Africa business.

What you'll do
• Define and maintain the target architecture for cross-border payments across the organisation
• Develop solution architectures for payment hubs, SWIFT, ISO 20022, clearing networks, correspondent banking and cross-border settlement processes
• Align technology solutions with enterprise architecture standards, the payment strategy and regulatory obligations
• Establish and enforce architectural principles, standards and governance processes for the payments domain
• Produce and continuously maintain conceptual, logical and physical architecture artefacts
• Act as the architecture authority for all cross-border payment initiatives on the platform
• Maintain end-to-end visibility of payment journeys across customer channels, core banking systems, payment hubs, middleware and external payment networks in the platform ecosystem
• Drive architecture decisions on SWIFT FIN and ISO 20022 messaging, cross-border payment processing, correspondent banking integrations, treasury and liquidity management integration, foreign exchange processing, sanctions and compliance screening, AML transaction monitoring, and real-time and near real-time payment capabilities
• Work with senior leadership to translate business objectives into technology strategies and architectural solutions
• Work with integrating capability areas to align solutions and architectural roadmaps

What you need
• 10+ years in architecture focused on payment solutions
• Financial banking experience
• SWIFT network experience (MX / MT)
• Agentic AI experience
• Enterprise Architect (Sparx) experience
• Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, engineering or a related field

Nice to have
• BIAN
• Cloud experience (AWS, Azure)
• TOGAF
• SWIFT-related qualifications
• PASA

Closing date: 2026-11-09

The Bank supports the recruitment and advancement of individuals with disabilities. In order for us to fulfill this purpose, candidates can disclose their disability information on a voluntary basis. The Bank will keep this information confidential unless we are required by law to disclose this information to other parties.

All appointments will be made in line with FirstRand Group’s Employment Equity plan.
